blocks.title: cut Silently Lies
items: Lines lacking the delimiter print WHOLE by default
`-s` suppresses them — usually what you wanted
cut never collapses repeated delimiters
Two spaces make an empty field: `cut -d' '` is near-always wrong
Space-aligned output: use `awk '{print $2}'` or `tr -s ' '` first
cut has zero quoting awareness
Real CSV with commas inside quotes defeats it
Reach for `csvcut` or python there, not a cleverer cut
tr reads ONLY stdin — it takes no file arguments
`tr '\n' ' '` joins lines into one

That split is the standard prelude to `sort | uniq -c`
No options means a full-line compare in locale collation order
`-u` dedupes by the sort key, not the whole line

caption.text: Most people learn grep, sed and awk as three unrelated spells — and then spend years debugging the same four silent corruptions. This handbook teaches them as one system: lines, fields, and filters joined by pipes, with the BRE/ERE inversion, the sed cycle, awk's strnum rule, and why `sort -k2` almost never means what you think. 10 pages, no filler — the version I wish someone had handed me before my first 500 GB log.
